```{r load_data, include=FALSE}
RGDP  <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "RGDP.Swiss.csv"))
UnEmp <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "UnEmp.Swiss.csv"))
Infl  <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "Inf.Swiss.csv"))
Int   <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "Int.Swiss.csv"))

RGDP  <- ts(RGDP$RGDP, frequency=4, start=c(1980,1))
UnEmp <- ts(UnEmp$UnEmp, frequency=4, start=c(2010,1))
Infl_qq <- ts(Infl$Infl, frequency=4, start=c(1960,1))  # raw q/q % change, not seasonally adjusted

# Seasonally adjusted, annualized inflation (400 x log difference).
# Rebuild a CPI index from the raw q/q rates, seasonally adjust it with X-13,
# and take annualized log differences.
CPI    <- ts(100 * cumprod(1 + Infl_qq / 100), frequency=4, start=c(1960,1))
CPI_sa <- final(seas(window(CPI, c(1990,1), c(2021,4))))
Infl   <- 400 * diff(log(CPI_sa))
Int   <- ts(Int$Int, frequency=4, start=c(1974,1))

# Real government final consumption expenditure, CHF, seasonally adjusted
# (OECD via FRED, series NAEXKP03CHQ652S); converted to millions of CHF to
# match RGDP
GovCons <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "GovCons_Real.Swiss.csv"))
GovCons <- ts(GovCons$NAEXKP03CHQ652S / 1e6, frequency=4, start=c(1980,1))
```

```{r helpers, include=FALSE}
fCreateDummyObs <- function(mY, vLambda, p){
  n <- ncol(mY)
  k <- n*p + 1
  vy <- apply(mY, 2, mean)
  vs <- apply(mY, 2, sd)
  mY_dummy <- diag(vs * vLambda[1])
  mX_dummy <- matrix(0, n, k)
  mX_dummy[, 2:(n+1)] <- diag(vs * vLambda[1])
  if (p > 1){
    for (ll in 2:p){
      mY_dummy_Here <- matrix(0, n, n)
      mX_dummy_Here <- matrix(0, n, k)
      mX_dummy_Here[, ((ll-1)*n + 2):(ll*n + 1)] <- diag(vs * vLambda[1] * ll^vLambda[2])
      mY_dummy <- rbind(mY_dummy, mY_dummy_Here)
      mX_dummy <- rbind(mX_dummy, mX_dummy_Here)
    }
  }
  mY_dummy_Here <- diag(vs)
  mX_dummy_Here <- matrix(0, n, k)
  for (ll in 1:vLambda[3]){
    mY_dummy <- rbind(mY_dummy, mY_dummy_Here)
    mX_dummy <- rbind(mX_dummy, mX_dummy_Here)
  }
  mY_dummy_Here <- diag(vy * vLambda[4])
  mX_dummy_Here <- matrix(0, n, k)
  for (ll in 1:p){
    mX_dummy_Here[, ((ll-1)*n + 2):(ll*n + 1)] <- diag(vy * vLambda[4])
  }
  mY_dummy <- rbind(mY_dummy, mY_dummy_Here)
  mX_dummy <- rbind(mX_dummy, mX_dummy_Here)
  mY_dummy_Here <- vy * vLambda[5]
  mX_dummy_Here <- c(vLambda[5], rep(vy * vLambda[5], times=p))
  mY_dummy <- rbind(mY_dummy, mY_dummy_Here)
  mX_dummy <- rbind(mX_dummy, mX_dummy_Here)
  return(list("mY_dummy"=mY_dummy, "mX_dummy"=mX_dummy))
}

fMinnesotaPriorParams <- function(mY, vLambda, p){
  n <- ncol(mY)
  k <- n*p + 1
  dummyObs <- fCreateDummyObs(mY, vLambda, p)
  mY_dummy <- dummyObs$mY_dummy
  mX_dummy <- dummyObs$mX_dummy
  mP <- t(mX_dummy) %*% mX_dummy
  mPhi <- solve(mP) %*% (t(mX_dummy) %*% mY_dummy)
  mErrors <- (mY_dummy - mX_dummy %*% mPhi)
  mS <- t(mErrors) %*% mErrors
  T_star <- nrow(mY_dummy)
  nu <- T_star - k
  return(list("mPhi"=mPhi, "mP"=mP, "mS"=mS, "nu"=nu))
}

fDataVARtoReg <- function(mY, T1, p){
  n <- ncol(mY)
  k <- n*p + 1
  Tall <- nrow(mY)
  mYY <- mY[T1:Tall, , drop=FALSE]
  mXX <- matrix(NA, nrow=(Tall-T1+1), ncol=k)
  mXX[, 1] <- 1
  for(i in 1:p){
    mXX[, ((i-1)*n + 2):(i*n + 1)] <- mY[(T1-i):(Tall-i), ]
  }
  return(list("mYY"=mYY, "mXX"=mXX))
}

fGetPosteriorMNIW <- function(mY, T1, p, mPhi_pr, mP_pr, mS_pr, nu_pr){
  RegData <- fDataVARtoReg(mY, T1, p)
  mYY <- RegData$mYY
  mXX <- RegData$mXX
  T <- nrow(mYY)
  mP_po <- mP_pr + t(mXX) %*% mXX
  mPhi_po <- solve(mP_po) %*% (mP_pr %*% mPhi_pr + t(mXX) %*% mYY)
  mS_po <- mS_pr + t(mPhi_pr) %*% mP_pr %*% mPhi_pr + t(mYY) %*% mYY -
           t(mPhi_po) %*% mP_po %*% mPhi_po
  nu_po <- nu_pr + T
  return(list("mPhi"=mPhi_po, "mP"=mP_po, "mS"=mS_po, "nu"=nu_po))
}

fGetMDD <- function(T, n, mPhi_pr, mP_pr, mS_pr, nu_pr,
                    mPhi_po, mP_po, mS_po, nu_po){
  logMDD <- -T*n/2 * log(pi) +
    n/2 * (-log(det(mP_po)) + log(det(mP_pr))) -
    nu_po/2 * log(det(mS_po)) + nu_pr/2 * log(det(mS_pr)) +
    CholWishart::lmvgamma(nu_po/2, n) - CholWishart::lmvgamma(nu_pr/2, n)
  return(logMDD)
}

fDrawMNIW <- function(M, mPhi, mP, mS, nu){
  k <- nrow(mPhi)
  n <- ncol(mPhi)
  vmu <- as.vector(mPhi)
  mPinv <- solve(mP)
  aSigma <- array(0, dim=c(n, n, M))
  aPhi <- array(0, dim=c(k, n, M))
  for (mm in 1:M){
    mSigmaHere <- MCMCpack::riwish(v=nu, S=mS)
    aSigma[, , mm] <- mSigmaHere
    vmuHere <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1, vmu, kronecker(mSigmaHere, mPinv))
    aPhi[, , mm] <- matrix(vmuHere, k, n)
  }
  return(list("Phi"=aPhi, "Sigma"=aSigma))
}

fVARIRF <- function(Phi_i, Sigma_i, q, Hmax, n, p){
  Sigma_tr <- t(chol(Sigma_i))
  IRFmat <- matrix(0, nrow=(Hmax+1), ncol=n)
  IRFmat[1, ] <- t(Sigma_tr %*% q)
  xxIRF <- matrix(0, nrow=1, ncol=p*n)
  xxIRF[1, 1:n] <- IRFmat[1, ]
  Phi_no_const <- Phi_i[2:(n*p+1), ]
  for(h in 1:Hmax){
    IRFmat[(1+h), ] <- xxIRF %*% Phi_no_const
    if(p > 1){
      xxIRF[1, (n+1):(n*p)] <- xxIRF[1, 1:(n*(p-1))]
    }
    xxIRF[1, 1:n] <- IRFmat[(1+h), ]
  }
  return(IRFmat)
}

# Standardize with the sample's own moments, then jointly pick the lag length
# p and lambda by MDD. All candidates are evaluated on the
# same estimation sample, starting at T1 = max(p_grid) + 2; the observations
# before T1 serve as the pre-sample for the Minnesota prior moments
# (Del Negro and Schorfheide, 2011). Uses only the data passed in, so it is safe to call
# recursively without look-ahead.
fFitBVAR <- function(mY_raw, p_grid, lambda_grid){
  T1 <- max(p_grid) + 2
  vMean <- apply(mY_raw, 2, mean)
  vSd   <- apply(mY_raw, 2, sd)
  mY <- sweep(sweep(mY_raw, 2, vMean, "-"), 2, vSd, "/")
  mY_pre <- mY[1:(T1-1), , drop=FALSE]
  n <- ncol(mY)
  T_data <- nrow(mY) - T1 + 1

  grid <- expand.grid(p = p_grid, l = seq_along(lambda_grid))
  grid$MDD <- mapply(function(p, l){
    pr <- fMinnesotaPriorParams(mY_pre, lambda_grid[[l]], p)
    po <- fGetPosteriorMNIW(mY, T1, p, pr$mPhi, pr$mP, pr$mS, pr$nu)
    fGetMDD(T_data, n, pr$mPhi, pr$mP, pr$mS, pr$nu,
            po$mPhi, po$mP, po$mS, po$nu)
  }, grid$p, grid$l)
  grid$lambda1 <- sapply(lambda_grid, `[`, 1)[grid$l]

  best <- grid[which.max(grid$MDD), ]
  p <- best$p
  vLambda <- lambda_grid[[best$l]]
  pr <- fMinnesotaPriorParams(mY_pre, vLambda, p)
  po <- fGetPosteriorMNIW(mY, T1, p, pr$mPhi, pr$mP, pr$mS, pr$nu)
  return(list("mY"=mY, "mean"=vMean, "sd"=vSd, "p"=p,
              "lambda"=vLambda, "grid"=grid[, c("p", "lambda1", "MDD")],
              "post"=po))
}

# Iterated h-step forecasts from the end of the fitted sample, in original
# units. With shocks=TRUE, draws from the full predictive distribution.
fForecastBVAR <- function(fit, H, M, shocks=FALSE){
  draws <- fDrawMNIW(M, fit$post$mPhi, fit$post$mP, fit$post$mS, fit$post$nu)
  n <- ncol(fit$mY)
  p <- fit$p
  Tn <- nrow(fit$mY)
  aFcst <- array(NA, dim=c(H, n, M))
  for (m in 1:M){
    Phi_m <- draws$Phi[, , m]
    mLags <- fit$mY[Tn:(Tn-p+1), , drop=FALSE]  # row 1 = most recent
    for (h in 1:H){
      y_h <- drop(c(1, t(mLags)) %*% Phi_m)
      if (shocks) y_h <- y_h + drop(mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1, sigma=draws$Sigma[, , m]))
      aFcst[h, , m] <- y_h
      mLags <- rbind(y_h, mLags)[1:p, , drop=FALSE]
    }
  }
  for (j in 1:n) aFcst[, j, ] <- aFcst[, j, ] * fit$sd[j] + fit$mean[j]
  return(list("draws"=aFcst, "mean"=apply(aFcst, c(1,2), mean)))
}
```

```{r data_prep, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# DATA PREPARATION: 2010 Q1 - 2020 Q4 (44 observations for training)
# ============================================================================
INT.ols  <- window(Int, c(2010,1), c(2020,4))
UR.ols   <- window(UnEmp, c(2010,1), c(2020,4))
INFL.ols <- window(Infl, c(2010,1), c(2020,4))

yyall <- cbind(INT.ols, UR.ols, INFL.ols)
colnames(yyall) <- c("INT", "UR", "INFL")
Tall <- nrow(yyall)
p_grid <- 1:4
n <- 3
M <- 1000

lambda_grid <- lapply(c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10),
                      function(l1) c(l1, 4, 1, 1, 1))

T1_forecast <- 13
```

```{r hyperparam_selection, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# HYPERPARAMETER SELECTION (full 2010-2020 sample, reported for reference)
# ============================================================================
fit_full <- fFitBVAR(yyall, p_grid, lambda_grid)
mdd_results <- fit_full$grid
vLambda_best <- fit_full$lambda
p <- fit_full$p
```

```{r forecasting, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# RECURSIVE ONE-STEP-AHEAD FORECASTS (2013 Q2 - 2020 Q4)
# At each origin t, standardization, lambda and posterior use data 1..t only.
# ============================================================================
T_start <- T1_forecast
T_end   <- Tall - 1
nFcst   <- T_end - T_start + 1

fcst_Bayesian <- matrix(NA, nFcst, n)
fcst_OLS      <- matrix(NA, nFcst, n)
fcst_RW       <- matrix(NA, nFcst, n)
actual        <- matrix(NA, nFcst, n)
lambda_path   <- rep(NA, nFcst)
p_path        <- rep(NA, nFcst)

set.seed(123)
for (t in T_start:T_end){
  i <- t - T_start + 1
  mY_t <- yyall[1:t, ]

  fit_t <- fFitBVAR(mY_t, p_grid, lambda_grid)
  fcst_Bayesian[i, ] <- fForecastBVAR(fit_t, 1, M)$mean[1, ]
  lambda_path[i] <- fit_t$lambda[1]
  p_path[i] <- fit_t$p

  # Flat-prior (OLS) VAR with the same lag length as the BVAR
  p_t <- fit_t$p
  # (not estimable when there are fewer observations than regressors)
  RegData_t <- fDataVARtoReg(mY_t, max(p_grid)+2, p_t)
  if (nrow(RegData_t$mXX) > ncol(RegData_t$mXX)){
    Phi_OLS_t <- solve(t(RegData_t$mXX) %*% RegData_t$mXX) %*%
                 (t(RegData_t$mXX) %*% RegData_t$mYY)
    fcst_OLS[i, ] <- c(1, t(mY_t[t:(t-p_t+1), , drop=FALSE])) %*% Phi_OLS_t
  }

  # Random walk: no-change forecast (Giannone, Lenza and Primiceri, 2015)
  fcst_RW[i, ] <- mY_t[t, ]

  actual[i, ] <- yyall[t + 1, ]
}

# Compare all models over the origins where the OLS VAR is estimable
common <- !is.na(fcst_OLS[, 1])
nCommon <- sum(common)
mse_Bayesian <- colMeans((fcst_Bayesian - actual)[common, , drop=FALSE]^2)
mse_OLS      <- colMeans((fcst_OLS - actual)[common, , drop=FALSE]^2)
mse_RW       <- colMeans((fcst_RW - actual)[common, , drop=FALSE]^2)
```

```{r forecast_2021, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# 2021 OUT-OF-SAMPLE FORECASTS: iterated 1- to 4-step-ahead from 2020 Q4
# ============================================================================
set.seed(3123)
fcst_2021 <- fForecastBVAR(fit_full, 4, M, shocks=TRUE)
fcst_2021_original <- fcst_2021$mean
fcst_2021_q05 <- apply(fcst_2021$draws, c(1,2), quantile, probs=0.05)
fcst_2021_q95 <- apply(fcst_2021$draws, c(1,2), quantile, probs=0.95)
colnames(fcst_2021_original) <- c("INT", "UR", "INFL")

actual_2021 <- cbind(
  as.numeric(window(Int, c(2021,1), c(2021,4))),
  as.numeric(window(UnEmp, c(2021,1), c(2021,4))),
  as.numeric(window(Infl, c(2021,1), c(2021,4)))
)
colnames(actual_2021) <- c("INT", "UR", "INFL")

rmse_2021 <- sqrt(colMeans((actual_2021 - fcst_2021_original)^2))
bias_2021 <- colMeans(actual_2021 - fcst_2021_original)
```

# Forecast Evaluation

```{r eval_table, results='asis'}
var_labels <- c("Interest Rate", "Unemployment", "Inflation")
cat("\\begin{table}[h!]\n\\centering\n")
cat(sprintf("\\caption{One-Step-Ahead Forecast MSE, Recursive Pseudo-Out-of-Sample (%d of %d forecasts 2013Q2--2020Q4 at which the OLS VAR is estimable)}\n", nCommon, nFcst))
cat("\\label{tab:forecast}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\n")
cat("\\textbf{Variable} & \\textbf{BVAR} & \\textbf{OLS VAR} & \\textbf{Random walk} & \\textbf{OLS / BVAR} & \\textbf{RW / BVAR} \\\\\n\\midrule\n")
for (j in 1:n){
  cat(sprintf("%s & %.3f & %.3f & %.3f & $%.1f\\times$ & $%.2f\\times$ \\\\\n",
              var_labels[j], mse_Bayesian[j], mse_OLS[j], mse_RW[j],
              mse_OLS[j] / mse_Bayesian[j], mse_RW[j] / mse_Bayesian[j]))
}
cat("\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n")

cat("\\begin{table}[h!]\n\\centering\n")
cat("\\caption{2021 Hold-Out: Iterated 1--4 Quarter Forecasts from 2020Q4}\n")
cat("\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\n")
cat("\\textbf{Variable} & \\textbf{RMSE} & \\textbf{Bias (actual $-$ forecast)} \\\\\n\\midrule\n")
for (j in 1:n){
  cat(sprintf("%s & %.3f & %.3f \\\\\n", var_labels[j], rmse_2021[j], bias_2021[j]))
}
cat("\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n")
```

MSEs are in original units (percentage points squared). Lag length and $\lambda_1$ are chosen jointly by MDD. On the full sample the optimum is $p =$ `r p`, $\lambda_1 =$ `r vLambda_best[1]`; across recursive origins $p$ ranges from `r min(p_path)` to `r max(p_path)` and $\lambda_1$ from `r min(lambda_path)` to `r max(lambda_path)`.

  time_axis <- time(yyall)[(T_start+1):Tall]

         main=paste(var_names[j], "| RMSE Bayes =", round(sqrt(mse_Bayesian[j]), 3),

    lines(time_axis, fcst_Bayesian[, j], col="red", lty=2, lwd=1.8)

    legend("topright", c("Actual", "Bayesian VAR", "OLS VAR"),
           col=c("steelblue", "red", "gray50"), lty=c(1,2,3), lwd=c(2.5,1.8,1.5), cex=0.9)
    grid(col="gray80", lty=3, lwd=0.5)
  }
})

# Monetary Policy Impulse Responses

A contractionary monetary policy shock is identified by sign restrictions on impact: the interest rate rises, unemployment rises, and inflation falls.

```{r monetary_irf, include=FALSE}
Hmax <- 16  # 4 years
set.seed(123)
postDraws <- fDrawMNIW(M, fit_full$post$mPhi, fit_full$post$mP,
                       fit_full$post$mS, fit_full$post$nu)

aIRF_sign_restricted <- array(NA, dim=c((Hmax+1), n, M))
max_attempts <- 1000

for(i in 1:M){
  Phi_i <- postDraws$Phi[, , i]
  Sigma_i <- postDraws$Sigma[, , i]
  for (attempt in 1:max_attempts){
    qtilde <- rnorm(n)
    q <- qtilde / sqrt(sum(qtilde^2))
    mIRF <- fVARIRF(Phi_i, Sigma_i, q, Hmax, n, p)
    if (mIRF[1, 1] < 0) mIRF <- -mIRF  # normalize to a rate increase
    if (mIRF[1, 2] > 0 && mIRF[1, 3] < 0){
      aIRF_sign_restricted[, , i] <- mIRF
      break
    }
  }
}

# Drop posterior draws with no rotation satisfying the restrictions
accepted <- !is.na(aIRF_sign_restricted[1, 1, ])
aIRF_sign_restricted <- aIRF_sign_restricted[, , accepted, drop=FALSE]

# Convert from standard-deviation units to percentage points
for (j in 1:n) aIRF_sign_restricted[, j, ] <- aIRF_sign_restricted[, j, ] * fit_full$sd[j]

mIRF_Mean <- apply(aIRF_sign_restricted, c(1,2), mean)
mIRF_q05  <- apply(aIRF_sign_restricted, c(1,2), quantile, probs=0.05)
mIRF_q95  <- apply(aIRF_sign_restricted, c(1,2), quantile, probs=0.95)
```

Responses use `r sum(accepted)` of `r M` posterior draws (draws with no admissible rotation after `r max_attempts` tries are dropped).

```{r monetary_plot, fig.height=5, fig.width=12}
fSaveFigure("monetary_irf.png", 12, 5, function(){
  par(mfrow=c(1, 3), mar=c(4, 4, 3, 2))
  var_names <- c("Interest Rate", "Unemployment", "Inflation")
  for(j in 1:n){
    plot(0:Hmax, mIRF_Mean[, j], type="l", col="blue", lwd=2.5,
         xlab="Horizon (quarters)", ylab=paste(var_names[j], "(pp)"),
         main=var_names[j], ylim=range(c(mIRF_q05[, j], mIRF_q95[, j], 0)))
    lines(0:Hmax, mIRF_q05[, j], col="red", lwd=1.5, lty=2)
    lines(0:Hmax, mIRF_q95[, j], col="red", lwd=1.5, lty=2)
    abline(h=0, col="black", lwd=0.8)
    grid()
  }
})
```

# Fiscal Shock Analysis

Following Blanchard and Perotti (2002), a recursively identified bivariate VAR(4) in quarterly log real government consumption and log real GDP with a constant and a linear time trend, spending ordered first so that it does not respond to other shocks within the quarter. The VAR is estimated by OLS/ML on the levels of the logs. Log responses are converted into CHF using the levels of spending and GDP in the last observation, and the multiplier is reported cumulatively.

```{r fiscal_data, include=FALSE}
fFiscalIRF <- function(start, end, Hmax, p = 4){
  GOV  <- log(window(GovCons, start, end))
  GDPR <- log(window(RGDP, start, end))
  yyall <- cbind(GOV, GDPR)
  Tall <- nrow(yyall)
  n  <- 2
  T1 <- p + 1

  # Regressors: constant, time trend, then y(t-1), ..., y(t-p)
  yy <- yyall[T1:Tall, ]
  xx <- matrix(1, nrow=(Tall-T1+1), ncol=(n*p+2))
  xx[, 2] <- 1:(Tall-T1+1)
  for (i in 1:p){
    xx[, (2+(i-1)*n+1):(2+i*n)] <- yyall[(T1-i):(Tall-i), ]
  }
  Phi_hat   <- solve(t(xx) %*% xx, t(xx) %*% yy)
  Sigma_hat <- (t(yy) %*% yy - t(yy) %*% xx %*% Phi_hat) / (Tall-T1+1)
  Sigma_hat_tr <- t(chol(Sigma_hat))

  # IRF to a one-standard-deviation spending shock
  IRFmat <- matrix(0, nrow=(Hmax+1), ncol=n)
  IRFmat[1, ] <- Sigma_hat_tr[, 1]
  xxIRF <- matrix(0, nrow=1, ncol=p*n)
  xxIRF[1, 1:n] <- IRFmat[1, ]
  Phi_hat_no_const <- Phi_hat[3:(n*p+2), , drop=FALSE]
  for (h in 1:Hmax){
    IRFmat[(1+h), ] <- xxIRF %*% Phi_hat_no_const
    if (p > 1) xxIRF[1, (n+1):(n*p)] <- xxIRF[1, 1:(n*(p-1))]
    xxIRF[1, 1:n] <- IRFmat[(1+h), ]
  }

  # Conversion into CHF at last-observation levels
  irfGOV_CHF  <- exp(GOV[Tall])  * IRFmat[, 1]
  irfGDPR_CHF <- exp(GDPR[Tall]) * IRFmat[, 2]

  return(list("irfG"=IRFmat[, 1], "irfY"=IRFmat[, 2],
              "multiplier"=irfGDPR_CHF / irfGOV_CHF,
              "multiplier_cum"=cumsum(irfGDPR_CHF) / cumsum(irfGOV_CHF),
              "GY_ratio"=exp(GOV[Tall] - GDPR[Tall]),
              "nobs"=Tall))
}

Hmax_fiscal <- 16  # quarters (4 years)
# Main estimate on the long pre-COVID sample;
# the project's 2010-2020 window is shown for comparison
fiscal_main  <- fFiscalIRF(c(1980,1), c(2019,4), Hmax_fiscal)
fiscal_short <- fFiscalIRF(c(2010,1), c(2020,4), Hmax_fiscal)
```

```{r fiscal_plots, fig.height=5, fig.width=12}
fSaveFigure("fiscal_irf.png", 12, 5, function(){
  par(mfrow=c(1, 3), mar=c(4, 4, 3, 2))
  h <- 0:Hmax_fiscal
  plot(h, fiscal_main$irfG * 100, type="o", col="darkblue", lwd=2.5, pch=16,
       xlab="Horizon (quarters)", ylab="Change (%)", main="Response of Gov Consumption",
       ylim=range(c(fiscal_main$irfG * 100, fiscal_short$irfG * 100, 0)))
  lines(h, fiscal_short$irfG * 100, type="o", col="gray50", lwd=1.5, pch=1, lty=2)
  legend("bottomleft", c("1980Q1-2019Q4 (main)", "2010Q1-2020Q4"), col=c("darkblue", "gray50"),
         lty=c(1, 2), pch=c(16, 1), cex=0.8)
  abline(h=0, col="red", lwd=1, lty=2)
  grid(col="gray80", lty=3)

  plot(h, fiscal_main$irfY * 100, type="o", col="darkgreen", lwd=2.5, pch=16,
       xlab="Horizon (quarters)", ylab="Change (%)", main="Response of Real GDP",
       ylim=range(c(fiscal_main$irfY * 100, fiscal_short$irfY * 100, 0)))
  lines(h, fiscal_short$irfY * 100, type="o", col="gray50", lwd=1.5, pch=1, lty=2)
  abline(h=0, col="red", lwd=1, lty=2)
  grid(col="gray80", lty=3)

  plot(h, fiscal_main$multiplier_cum, type="o", col="purple", lwd=2.5, pch=16,
       xlab="Horizon (quarters)", ylab="CHF GDP per CHF spending",
       main="Cumulative Fiscal Multiplier (1980-2019)",
       ylim=range(c(fiscal_main$multiplier_cum, 0, 1)))
  abline(h=c(0, 1), col=c("red", "gray60"), lwd=1, lty=c(2, 3))
  grid(col="gray80", lty=3)
})
```

The main estimate uses `r fiscal_main$nobs` quarters from 1980 to 2019; the gray lines re-estimate the same specification on the project's `r fiscal_short$nobs`-quarter 2010--2020 window. In that short sample the cumulative spending response returns to zero within four years, so the CHF multiplier ratio is not meaningful there and is not plotted. Government consumption is about `r round(100 * fiscal_main$GY_ratio)`% of GDP, which is why a modest percentage response of GDP translates into a sizable CHF multiplier.

## Data Sources

- **Interest Rate (INT):** Swiss 3-month LIBOR, from FRED / ECB.
- **Unemployment (UR):** Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), seasonally adjusted. https://www.seco.admin.ch/
- **Inflation (INFL):** Swiss CPI, Swiss National Bank (SNB). The raw quarter-on-quarter changes are converted into a price index, seasonally adjusted with X-13ARIMA-SEATS (1990--2021), and expressed as annualized quarter-on-quarter log changes ($400 \times \Delta \log$ CPI).
- **Real GDP:** Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO). https://www.bfs.admin.ch/
- **Government consumption:** real general government final consumption expenditure, seasonally adjusted (OECD Main Economic Indicators via FRED, series NAEXKP03CHQ652S).

All data are publicly available from the sources listed above and are included in `Data/`.
